title: Side-Channel Attack Surface
description: An interactive SVG infographic of a CPU performing a crypto operation while leaking its secret key through four physical side channels — timing, power/EM, cache, and rowhammer — each reaching an attacker, with hover tooltips giving real-world examples and a defenses badge.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

learningObjectives: Identify the four major classes of hardware side channel.
Explain that a secret leaks through physical side effects, not the logical interface.
Match a defense to each side-channel class.

instructionalStrategies: Hover each channel to read its real-world example, then connect it to the matching defense in the badge.
Ask students why a logically correct, bug-free implementation can still leak the key.

assessmentQuestions.question: Why does constant-time code defend the timing channel but not the power channel?
A cloud tenant shares a physical host with an attacker VM. Which channel is most relevant and why?
